source_acquisition.search_note: PDF 的正文、脚注、references 和元数据没有作者 GitHub/project/code URL；抽取文本中仅见 proceedings URL。gh 只读标题/作者/arXiv 检索找到一个同名但为空的 stemvibe 仓库，以及 MachineLearning-Nerd/icml26-grokking。后者 README/SOURCE_AUDIT 明确写出完整标题、arXiv 2601.19791 和 OpenReview 5nNNVY8NW4，树中有 v3 paper source archive、LaTeX 和全部 19 个 plot PNG。该仓库是独立 reproduction，快照为 v3，目标 PDF 是 v4；但 19/19 个 PDF 嵌入 RGB 图像与对应 PNG 逐像素一致，因此采用 asset-level exact source。仓库没有 plot-generating Python、rcParams、TikZ/PGF 或 table generator；图内字体/字号/线宽仍为 200 dpi rendered estimate，未把 independent reproduction 脚本当作原作者视觉源。

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figure 1/3/5/6/7 mostly use pure blue #0000FF, red #FF0000, and light coral #FFA07A; Figures 2/4 use blue/red for t₁/t₂ and green #008000/orange #FFA500 for error bars. Figure 1 adds translucent pink #FFCCD5 and blue/purple #887BD7/#8871CE bands. Grid lines are gray dashed and backgrounds white. Train/test is often redundantly encoded by dashed/solid, but Figure 1 uses two solid colors and Figures 2/4 switch color semantics to t₁/t₂.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: All 19 plot panels are embedded RGB raster PNGs with soft masks; captions, axes outside the image, and body text are PDF text/vector objects. No Table or vector chart object appears in the target PDF. Source TeX gives includegraphics dimensions, but no plot-generation style file is public.
paper_style.style_consistency: Figures 1–4 use small-column 2-panel/2×2 raster layouts in the ICML body; Figures 5–7 use page-width or inset appendix layouts. Log training-step axes, grid lines, and train/test line grammar recur, while panel scales and t₁/t₂ versus loss color semantics vary. Low-resolution 600×400 assets in Figures 2/4 are visibly less legible than the high-resolution assets.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Comparing training and test squared losses using GD with weight decay over 50 independent runs (with independent datasets and student initializations). Left: training a ridge regression model to learn the zero teacher; Right: training a two-layer ReLU neural network (training both layers) to learn the zero teacher. We scale the x-axis logarithmically, which is commonly adopted for plotting the grokking phenomenon (Power et al., 2022; Lyu et al., 2024; Xu et al., 2024; Mohamadi et al., 2024). See Section 5 for further details of the experimental setup.

color.semantic_mapping: Red #FF0000 is training loss and blue #0000FF is test loss; translucent pink #FFCCD5 and blue/purple #887BD7/#8871CE bands show cross-run spread, but the caption does not define the aggregation.

encodings.x: training steps on a logarithmic axis, approximately 10^0–10^6
encodings.y: training/test square loss on a linear axis
encodings.color: red=training, blue=test; translucent bands around both curves
encodings.line: solid curves for both training and test
encodings.facet: left=ridge regression zero teacher; right=two-layer ReLU zero teacher
encodings.text: legend labels training loss and test loss; axis labels

figures.data_and_statistics: The caption reports 50 independent runs with independent datasets and student initializations. Each panel compares training and test squared loss over logarithmic training steps. The central curve aggregation, band statistic, test-population construction, and per-time denominator are not specified; panel hyperparameters are given in Section 5 rather than the caption.
figures.evidence_relation: The p. 2 §1 three-stage grokking motivation (early overfit, persistent poor test performance, eventual recovery) points to Figure 1 as an illustration; the two model panels then lead into §5 Figures 2–4 and §6 scope discussion. The plot is illustrative evidence, not a replacement for the ridge theorems.
design_strengths: Places ridge and fully trained ReLU trajectories on a common train/test and log-time grammar in the introduction.
Uses 50-run bands to expose trajectory spread instead of presenting only one idealized curve.
Keeps the two-panel comparison simple enough to identify delayed test improvement quickly.
design_weaknesses: The band has no definition of mean/median or interval, so its uncertainty meaning is not auditable.
Panel-specific settings are deferred to Section 5 and the two panels have different y ranges, making cross-panel comparison primarily qualitative.
Overlapping pink and purple bands blend visually and the downscaled tick/legend text is small; no line-style redundancy distinguishes the two losses.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a shared log-time train/test line grammar to introduce a canonical phenomenon and a model extension; if cross-run bands are shown, state the aggregation, interval definition, denominator, and panel settings in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. Plots for the effects of hyperparameters on grokking in ridge regression. Left Upper: decreasing weight decay extends the generalization delay (t₂ ∝ 1/λ); Right Upper: decreasing sample size amplifies grokking by speeding up the convergence of the training loss (affects t₁); Left Lower: increasing the feature dimension has little effect on t₁ and t₂; Right Lower: increasing the initialization scale increases t₁ and t₂ simultaneously at logarithmic rates (t₁, t₂ ∝ ln(ν²)).

color.semantic_mapping: Blue #0000FF encodes t₁, red #FF0000 encodes t₂; green #008000 and orange #FFA500 are the small t₁/t₂ error bars. Solid/dashed and x/circle markers distinguish empirical/theory and t₁/t₂.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: panel-specific: lower-left in λ; upper-right or lower-right in the other panels

encodings.x: λ, n, m, or ν² sweep per panel; λ/n/ν² are power/log-spaced and m is linear
encodings.y: t₁ and t₂ training steps; first three panels use powers-of-two log ticks and ν² uses linear ×10^4
encodings.text: panel titles, four-entry legends, power/scientific tick labels

figures.data_and_statistics: The figure compares Equation (8) theoretical bounds (dashed) with empirically observed t₁/t₂ (solid). λ, n, and m panels show about five sweep points each; ν² shows about seven, for approximately 88 primary marks in total. No run count, seed, error-bar definition, aggregation rule, or test-population denominator is reported.
figures.evidence_relation: Theorems 4.2 and 4.4–4.6 plus Eq. (8) predict t₁/t₂ dependence; Figure 2 is the direct theory-versus-observation interface. The p. 7 §5.1 prose defines dashed bounds and solid observations, after which Figures 3–4 test directional transfer to ReLU models.
design_strengths: Splits the same t₁/t₂ estimands over λ, n, m, and ν² in four aligned small multiples, directly matching the theoretical control variables.
Uses solid/dashed, marker shape, color, and error bars as partially redundant encodings of theory/empirical and t₁/t₂.
Caption states the directional conclusion for every panel instead of leaving the reader to infer all slopes.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not define error bars, repeats, marker semantics, or panel-specific linear/log scales; visual proximity is not formal calibration evidence.
600×400 assets become cramped at 3.5 cm, with tiny legend, ticks, and error bars.
Mixed scales and different y magnitudes make absolute cross-panel height comparisons invalid, especially the ν² scientific-notation panel.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a 2×2 small-multiple interface for one pair of estimands across multiple theoretical controls; retain solid/dashed, marker, and error-bar redundancy and state each panel’s scale, sweep values, repeats, and uncertainty definition.

evidence.label: Figure 2; §5.1 “dashed lines represent our theoretical bounds”

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. Plots of training and test losses of a two-layer random ReLU features network. Dashed/solid lines indicate train/test loss respectively. Left Upper: using smaller weight decay amplifies the grokking time by delaying generalization (increases t₂); Right Upper: having smaller sample size amplifies grokking by speeding up the training convergence (decreases t₁); Left Lower: increasing the student’s width does not significantly prolong grokking; Left Lower: increasing the initialization scale does not significantly prolong grokking, but instead widens the gap between the generalization and training losses during the overfitting stage.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue, red, and light coral encode the three values of each swept hyperparameter; dashed/solid line style encodes training/test.

encodings.color: three sweep levels per panel: blue, red, light coral
encodings.facet: 2×2 panels: λ, n, m, ν² tuning
encodings.text: panel title and six-entry legend identify sweep value and loss role

figures.data_and_statistics: Each panel contains six trajectories: dashed training and solid test for three levels of λ (about 10^-4/10^-5/10^-6), n (100/200/500), m (1000/10000/100000), or ν² (1/5/10). There are about seven sampled training-step positions per trace, approximately 168 marks overall. The teacher is sampled independently of the student, so the paper labels this a non-realizable setting; no repeats or uncertainty are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 2’s ridge prediction is reused as a visual grammar for a fixed-hidden-layer random-ReLU extension. Section 5.2 p. 8 explicitly calls the teacher/student pair non-realizable and says its behavior is similar to realizable ridge; §6 then leaves a non-realizable ridge proof as an open question.
design_strengths: Preserves Figure 2’s λ/n/m/ν² panel order so directional transfer across model families can be scanned without relearning the layout.
Stable dashed/solid train/test coding plus three hue levels makes the delayed separation of training and test loss visible in every panel.
High-resolution 2500×1200 assets preserve axes and curves better than the small Figure 4 assets.
design_weaknesses: The caption repeats “Left Lower” for the initialization panel, breaking panel navigation.
Exact sweep values, repeats, and non-realizability are not fully encoded in the figure; the reader must consult §5.2.
Light coral is weak in grayscale/projection and has no marker/direct-label redundancy for parameter level.
figures.reusable_pattern: Reuse one 2×2 hyperparameter grammar when testing directional transfer from a proved model to an empirical extension; reserve line style for train/test, discrete colors for sweep level, and state the extension boundary and uncertainty protocol.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4. Plots for the effect of the hyperparameters on grokking when training a two-layer ReLU network with the zero teacher.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue #0000FF is t₁, red #FF0000 is t₂; green #008000 and orange #FFA500 are t₁/t₂ error bars. Both main series use x markers and solid lines.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: panel-specific: upper-right or lower-right depending on panel

encodings.x: λ, n, m, or ν² sweep; λ/n/ν² are power/log-spaced and m is linear
encodings.y: t₁/t₂ training steps; first three panels use powers-of-two log ticks and ν² uses linear ×10^5
encodings.shape: x marker for both t₁ and t₂
encodings.line: solid for both t₁ and t₂
encodings.facet: 2×2 panels: λ, n, m, ν² dependence
encodings.text: panel titles, two-entry legends, power/scientific tick labels

figures.data_and_statistics: The figure summarizes t₁ and t₂ for a fully trained two-layer ReLU zero teacher while sweeping λ, n, m, and ν². λ has about six points, n and m about five each, and ν² about seven, for approximately 46 marks; error-bar definitions, seeds, repeats, and baseline/theory curves are absent.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 2’s linear/ridge t₁/t₂ dependence is the reference; Figure 4 is the both-layers-trained ReLU extension. Section 5.3 p. 8 says the dependencies match qualitatively and §6 frames this as a stepping stone, not a nonlinear theorem.
design_strengths: Shares λ/n/m/ν² small-multiple structure with Figure 2, making the qualitative extension comparison direct.
Point markers and error bars distinguish summary times from the loss trajectories in Figure 3.
Compact 2×2 layout fits extension evidence into the main text while exposing the flat m effect and strong ν² effect.
design_weaknesses: 600×400 assets make axes, legends, and small error bars difficult to read at 3.5 cm.
The caption does not define t₁/t₂, marker/colour/error-bar semantics, scales, sweep values, or repeats; it is not independently auditable.
Both series use the same marker and solid line, so t₁/t₂ rely mainly on color; no theory or baseline curve quantifies “qualitative match.”
figures.reusable_pattern: Put extension-model summary times in the same panel order as the theory figure, but provide per-point definitions, repeat counts, uncertainty statistics, and panel-specific scale notes in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5. Plotting the grokking by evaluating the surrogate loss (an accuracy-type metric) compared to evaluating the actual loss. The data for the two plots are collected from a single simulation. We set m = 10000, d = 100, n = 100, η = 1, λ = 10⁻⁵ and ϵ = 0.01.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue is used for both metrics; dashed/solid line style distinguishes training/test and panel y labels distinguish accuracy from square loss.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: upper-left in accuracy panel; upper-right in square-loss panel

encodings.y: left=threshold surrogate accuracy; right=actual square loss, both linear
encodings.facet: left accuracy versus right square loss
encodings.text: legends and y-axis labels identify metric and loss role

figures.data_and_statistics: Both panels use one simulation with m=10000, d=100, n=100, η=1, λ=10^-5, and ε=0.01. The left metric is P_x((N(x;θ^(t))−N*(x))²≤ε), producing a visible plateau before late test improvement; the right squared loss declines smoothly. There are no repeated runs or uncertainty estimates.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 6 distinguishes a classification-like plateau from continuous regression loss; Appendix B defines the threshold surrogate and Figure 5 places the two evaluations on the same trajectory. The panel pair supports a metric-dependent mechanism claim, not a new grokking theorem.
design_strengths: Uses the same log-time and train/test grammar while changing only the evaluation metric, isolating the source of the plateau visually.
Caption includes the threshold, model dimensions, optimizer settings, and explicit single-simulation boundary.
Single-color line-style coding remains legible in grayscale.
design_weaknesses: One simulation has no uncertainty and cannot establish plateau stability across initialization or data draws.
The two y axes have different units and ranges, so vertical heights are not comparable across panels.
Sparse unmarked time points make exact threshold-crossing times hard to verify, and the legend overlays plotting whitespace.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a threshold/surrogate metric with its continuous counterpart on a shared log-time layout, and explicitly label the metric-dependent interpretation plus single-versus-repeated evidence boundary.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6. Ridge regression with label noise — Left: We set m = 5000, d = 50, n = 100, η = 1, std = 0.1 and λ = 10⁻⁵; Right: We notice that different noise levels do not affect the grokking time by much. We set m = 5000, d = 50, n = 100, η = 1, and λ = 10⁻⁵.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue, red, and light coral encode std=0.01, 0.05, and 0.1; dashed/solid line style encodes training/test.

encodings.color: three label-noise levels: blue=.01, red=.05, light coral=.1
encodings.facet: left fixed std=.1; right three-noise-level comparison
encodings.text: left two-entry and right six-entry legends identify noise/loss combinations

figures.data_and_statistics: The left panel fixes std=0.1 with m=5000, d=50, n=100, η=1, λ=10^-5. The right panel compares std=.01, .05, .1 while holding the other settings fixed. Training/test square-loss traces share a log x axis; no run count, seed, uncertainty, threshold definition, or repetition is reported.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 6 names non-realizable ridge with label noise as an open theoretical direction; Appendix B supplies this observation. Figure 6 complements Figure 3’s random-feature non-realizable traces but does not close the non-realizable theorem gap.
design_strengths: Pairs a canonical fixed-noise trajectory with a nuisance-level sweep in one page-width object.
Right legend explicitly enumerates each noise/train-test combination and line style remains stable across levels.
Caption states concrete m/d/n/η/λ/std settings and a bounded qualitative claim.
design_weaknesses: “Do not affect the grokking time by much” has no defined estimator, tolerance, repeat count, or statistical comparison.
Six traces and a long right legend consume plotting area; light coral has weak contrast and noise level relies on color.
A single appendix observation cannot establish a noisy-ridge theorem or reveal failure/exception counts.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a fixed canonical panel plus a nuisance-level sweep, but define the noise unit, time threshold, repeats, aggregation, and acceptable difference before calling the object robustness evidence.

evidence.label: Figure 6; Appendix B “different noise levels do not affect the grokking time by much”

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7. Random Fourier features — we set m = 5000, d = 10, n = 100, η = 1, σ² = 1 and λ = 10⁻⁴.

color.semantic_mapping: Single blue #0000FF is shared by training/test; dashed/solid line style carries the role distinction.

encodings.text: title RFF, legend, and axis labels

figures.data_and_statistics: This is one RFF realizable-teacher trajectory with m=5000, d=10, n=100, η=1, σ²=1, λ=10^-4. Training loss falls early while test loss remains high until late training; no run count, seed, error, repeat, or tuning-failure rate is given.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix B describes the RFF map and same-distribution realizable teacher before Figure 7. The object sits beside Figures 5–6 as an additional feature-family observation; the body warns that careful hyperparameter tuning is needed, so it is not a general theorem or stability result.
design_strengths: Low-complexity single panel makes the delayed RFF trajectory easy to scan.
Wide 0.75-column asset provides larger tick and legend text than the small Figure 2/4 panels.
Single-color plus line-style grammar is grayscale-friendly and consistent with the other loss traces.
design_weaknesses: No repeated realizations or uncertainty are shown, so stability of this RFF example is unknown.
Caption omits dashed/solid semantics, squared-loss/test-population details, and the tuning range or failure rate alluded to in the body.
Sparse points and substantial whitespace make an exact grokking-time crossing difficult to read.
figures.reusable_pattern: For a new feature family, retain a single canonical train/test trace but put the feature map, teacher realizability, tuning protocol, failure rate, and repetition uncertainty next to the figure.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 introduces delayed generalization in ridge and ReLU; Figure 2 makes the ridge theory’s t₁/t₂ hyperparameter dependence observable; Figures 3–4 transfer the same panel order to random-feature and fully trained ReLU models; Appendix Figures 5–7 test metric dependence, label-noise variation, and a random Fourier feature family. The chain is theory mechanism → quantitative control → empirical extension → bounded additional evidence.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All captions use Figure n. below the raster object. Figures 1/3/6 explain settings and comparisons; Figure 3 explicitly defines dashed/solid train/test, while Figures 2/4 rely on body prose for line/marker/error semantics. Figure 5/7 are parameter-list captions, and Figure 4 is only a generic title. No caption defines run-level uncertainty or error-bar statistics.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: The PDF contains no Table object, so there is no table header hierarchy, row-group, rule, precision, or highlighting system to audit.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Theorem 4.2 and Theorems 4.4–4.6 plus Eq. (8) connect to Figure 2’s dashed theory/solid empirical t₁/t₂ comparison. Figures 3–4 reuse the hyperparameter grammar for empirical nonlinear extensions and should be read as robustness/qualitative evidence rather than component-deletion ablations. Figures 5–7 are Appendix B additional experiments, not new theorem validation.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Figures 1–4 are main-text objects on pp. 2, 7, and 8. Section 6 explicitly points to Appendix B label-noise evidence (Figure 6); Appendix B on pp. 22–23 contains Figures 5–7, with Figure 5 following the surrogate-metric definition and Figures 6–7 following the noise/RFF descriptions.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Plot interiors are rasterized and visually use a consistent sans-serif Matplotlib style, while captions/body use Nimbus Roman and Computer Modern. The small 600×400 panels have lower effective type size than the 1500×1200/2500×1200 panels; all exact plot-font claims remain estimates because no plotting source code is available.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/red recur across loss traces, but in Figures 2/4 they encode t₁/t₂ rather than training/test; green/orange are reserved for summary-time error bars and light coral for a third sweep/noise level. Line style and marker redundancy helps, but Figure 1 and parts of Figure 6 rely more heavily on hue/band luminance.

most_reusable_patterns: Use a shared log-time train/test trace grammar from an introduction canonical example through metric/noise/feature-family appendices.
Use 2×2 small multiples for one pair of estimands across λ, n, m, and ν²; Figure 2’s theory/empirical line styles and t₁/t₂ markers are the strongest summary-time grammar.
Keep panel order and axis semantics stable when transferring a mechanism from ridge regression to random-feature and fully trained ReLU models.
Add line-style/marker redundancy and put sweep values, scale choice, repeat count, and uncertainty definition in captions so raster objects remain auditable outside the body.
highest_value_objects: Figure 2: the direct visual interface between Eq. (8) theory and empirical t₁/t₂ hyperparameter control.
Figure 1: the clearest introduction headline for the canonical delayed-generalization phenomenon and its ReLU analogue.
Figure 5: a structurally informative metric-dependent plateau comparison, bounded by one simulation.
Figures 3–4: matched empirical extensions from ridge to random-feature/full-trained ReLU, useful when read as qualitative rather than theorem evidence.
failure_patterns: Figures 2/4 mix panel scales without caption-level explanation, and low-resolution 600×400 assets make legend/ticks/error bars hard to read.
Figures 1–4 defer band, line, marker, error-bar, repeat, and sweep-setting definitions to body prose; Figure 4 is especially non-self-contained.
Figure 3 repeats “Left Lower”; Figure 4 has only a generic caption; Figure 7 does not define dashed/solid train/test.
Figures 1, 3, 5, 6, and 7 lack auditable run-level uncertainty, while Figures 5/7 are single-realization or single-simulation evidence.
Appendix qualitative traces cannot replace the missing non-realizable or nonlinear end-to-end proof; visual agreement in Figure 2 cannot replace formal error analysis.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use fixed log-time train/test traces and an isomorphic 2×2 hyperparameter grammar to carry the training–delayed-generalization–recovery story from proved ridge dynamics into metric, noise, and feature-family observations while keeping uncertainty and nonlinear scope explicit in text.
